Article Title: 'I am not taking it for granted': Vaibhav Sooryavanshi after breaking Sachin Tendulkar's record
Article Text:
Vaibhav Sooryavanshi (ANI Photo)

Poll Vote & Share your view Do you think performance of Vaibhav Sooryavanshi against Zimbabwe will influence his future matches? Yes, it will boost his confidence. No, he might still feel pressure. 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

Vaibhav Sooryavanshi believes his record-breaking maiden international half-century has given him the confidence he needs after a difficult start to life in international cricket.The 15-year-old announced his arrival in style by smashing an 18-ball fifty against Zimbabwe in the opening T20I in Harare on Thursday, becoming the youngest player to score a half-century in men's international cricket.The knock marked a dramatic turnaround for the teenage opener, who had endured a disappointing debut series against England. Sooryavanshi managed just 42 runs across his first three T20I innings, scoring 14 off 10 balls, 13 off five deliveries and 15 off 10 balls.After helping India secure a seven-wicket victory over Zimbabwe and a 1-0 lead in the three-match series, Sooryavanshi said the innings would play a key role in boosting his self-belief at the start of his international journey."When you are in the starting phase of your career, and you get such an innings at the start, you get confidence for the next matches. It felt like I was in my zone and I backed my own strength," Sooryavanshi said in a video posted by the BCCI.At 15 years and 118 days, Sooryavanshi eclipsed a long-standing record held by Sachin Tendulkar . The Indian batting legend was 16 years and 213 days old when he scored his maiden international fifty against Pakistan in the Faisalabad Test in 1989.Harare has become a particularly memorable venue for the youngster. Earlier this year, he lit up the same ground with a breathtaking 175 off 80 balls against England in the final of the 2026 Under-19 World Cup. Months later, he returned to the venue to produce another innings that underlined his immense potential.Despite enjoying success in Harare, Sooryavanshi insisted he is not taking any venue or opportunity for granted and remains focused on making meaningful contributions wherever he plays."There are some grounds where you like to make runs. I am not taking it for granted. I am just trying to play wherever I can, give my best, contribute to the team and do well," he said.The teenager also acknowledged the role played by those who have supported him throughout his rise, dedicating the milestone to his family and coaches."I will dedicate myself to my family, to my coaches, to everyone who supported me in my journey," he concluded.Sooryavanshi's explosive knock laid the foundation for India's comfortable chase of Zimbabwe's 125 for seven, with the visitors sealing victory by seven wickets and taking an early advantage in the three-match T20I series.
Article Summary: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi becomes youngest player to score a half-century in men's international cricket. The 15-year-old smashed an 18-ball fifty against Zimbabwe in the opening T20I in Harare on Thursday. India secure a seven-wicket victory over Zimbabwe and a 1-0 lead in the three-match series.

Article Title: Ashes in India? Cricket Australia leaves door open for landmark 150th Test
Article Text:
Steve Smith, left, and Ben Stokes pose for a photo with Ashes Trophy (AP photo)

Cricket Australia chief executive Todd Greenberg has said the board would be open to exploring the possibility of staging the landmark 150th anniversary Ashes Test in India, underlining the growing importance of the Indian market to world cricket.Australia and England are scheduled to play a one-off Test in March next year to commemorate 150 years of the historic Ashes rivalry. While there are no current plans to take the match outside Australia, Greenberg admitted the idea of hosting it in India could be considered in the future.His comments come at a time when Cricket Australia is expanding its footprint in India. This December, the Big Bash League will stage a match in Chennai, where Melbourne Renegades will face Perth Scorchers, marking another step in bringing Australian cricket closer to Indian fans.The prospect of an Ashes Test in India also reflects the commercial significance of the country's cricket market. India remains the sport's biggest audience, and hosting a marquee contest between Australia and England would generate enormous interest while creating fresh commercial opportunities.Greenberg said Cricket Australia would not rule out the idea, citing its strong ties with both the England and Wales Cricket Board (ECB) and the Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI)."We'd have to be open to consider all options," Greenberg told the BBC's Stumped podcast. "Our relationship with the ECB, but also the BCCI, is very strong. And clearly, there are opportunities in India to put more content into certain areas. That's not something we are currently planning, but it would certainly be open for consideration."India's influence on the global cricket economy has continued to grow in recent years. The ECB, for instance, is expected to post substantial profits from the eight white-ball internationals it hosted against India recently, despite England winning six of those matches. The financial returns are expected to surpass what the board anticipates from staging both the men's and women's Ashes series next year.Despite his openness to the proposal, Greenberg acknowledged that scheduling a five-day Ashes Test in India would be far from straightforward.The Indian calendar is already packed with international cricket and the IPL, which is expected to begin earlier than usual next year to avoid the extreme heat towards the end of May. Finding a suitable window for another marquee event would therefore be a major challenge."I think Test cricket between us, England and India, is still very strong, probably bucking the trend as to other parts of the world. So we want to make sure we continue to grow it and strengthen it."The challenge for all of us in global cricket is there are only 365 days in a schedule, and we probably need another month or two if we actually can generate the content we want to," he said.
Article Summary: Cricket Australia chief executive Todd Greenberg says the board would be open to exploring the possibility of staging the landmark 150th anniversary Ashes Test in India. Australia and England are scheduled to play a one-off Test in March next year to commemorate 150 years of the historic Ashes rivalry.

Article Title: Indian flavour at glittering 2026 Commonwealth Games opening ceremony
Article Text:
The team from India arrives on stage during the Commonwealth Games opening ceremony in Glasgow, Scotland, Thursday, July 23, 2026. (AP Photo/Kin Cheung)

GLASGOW: The jingle of ‘ghungroos’ — anklets strung with tiny metallic bells — blended with singer Callum Beattie’s rendition of ‘Yes Sir, I Can Boogie’ as six Indian dancers lit up the OVO Hydro during Thursday’s opening ceremony of the 23rd Commonwealth Games.The ‘Parade of Nations’ came early in the show, introducing each participating country and its athletes. With Scotland home to a sizeable South Asian community, India was clearly among the crowd favourites. Mirabai Chanu , carrying the tricolour and Lovlina Borgohain, bearing the King’s Baton, led the Indian contingent into the arena to roaring applause.Dynamic LED lighting, projection mapping and immersive effects transformed the arena into a mesmerising spectacle. It was the first opening ceremony in Commonwealth Games history to be staged indoors.Shortly after the clock sequence, the crowd erupted as the six-member, Glasgowbased troupe ‘The Ghungroo Revolution’ took the stage. Three dancers in pink Banarasi dupattas swirled to Kathak rhythms, while the other three, dressed in green sarees and temple jewellery, delivered a power-packed Bharatanatyam performance. Every movement of the classical form, rooted in Tamil Nadu’s temple traditions, was executed with grace and precision.Speaking to TOI about the journey to the Games stage, troupe founder Kamalika Ghosh said, “It was quite a rigorous process. We had to go through several rounds of auditions. In fact, even explaining the difference between Kathak and Bharatanatyam to the organisers was a challenge.”Ghosh, a technology professional, added, “Our troupe finally made the cut from among hundreds of applicants. Then came the rehearsals, with hours and hours of back-breaking practice.” All six members — Kamalika, Shilpi, Triparna, Gayathri, Ankita and Pratiksha — have full-time jobs.Triparna Mukherjee, a mother of one and a debt recovery professional with Intrum, specialises in Kathak. “Balancing family, a job and a passion is not easy. We had to carve out time for rehearsals every day of the week, but I must say the organisers’ professionalism was topnotch,” she said.
Article Summary: The six-member, Glasgowbased troupe ‘The Ghungroo Revolution’ took the stage. Three dancers in pink Banarasi dupattas swirled to Kathak rhythms. The other three, dressed in green sarees and temple jewellery, delivered a power-packed Bharatanatyam performance.

Article Title: Historic! South Africa's Chad le Clos scripts Commonwealth Games record, becomes its most decorated male athlete
Article Text:
Chad le Clos of Team South Africa (Photo by Quinn Rooney/Getty Images)

A career full of milestones

South African swimmer Chad le Clos made history on Friday by becoming the most decorated male athlete in Commonwealth Games history after helping his team win bronze in the men's 4x100m freestyle relay.The medal was the 19th Commonwealth Games medal of his career, taking him ahead of Australian shooter Phil Adams and England's Mick Gault.“I shouldn’t be crying at bronze, I should be crying at gold, but honestly this means the world,” the 34-year-old Le Clos said on the Games website. With this latest achievement, his Commonwealth medal tally now stands at seven golds, four silvers and eight bronzes.Le Clos could still add to his record as he is also set to compete in the 50m and 100m butterfly events.He first appeared at the Commonwealth Games in 2010 in New Delhi, where, at just 18 years old, he won five medals. The current edition marks his fifth appearance at the Games.Beyond the Commonwealth stage, Le Clos has enjoyed a remarkable international career. He has won four Olympic medals, including one gold, and claimed 16 world championship titles, mainly in the butterfly events.The veteran swimmer has also set his sights on competing at a fifth Olympic Games when Los Angeles hosts the event in 2028.
Article Summary: South African swimmer Chad le Clos becomes most decorated male athlete in Commonwealth Games history. Le Clos helped his team win bronze in the men's 4x100m freestyle relay. The medal was the 19th Commonwealth Games medal of his career.

Article Title: Commonwealth Games: Jhandu Kumar wins India's first medal in para powerlifting; day 2 brings mixed results in Glasgow
Article Text:
Jhandu Kumar celebrates after winning the bronze medal during the medal ceremony for the men's heavyweight para powerlifting event at the Commonwealth Games 2026, in Glasgow. (PTI Photo)

Jhandu Kumar wins India's first medal

Ashok Malik finishes fourth

Karthik Budigina misses podium in para swimming

Jadumani Singh enters pre-quarterfinals

Srihari Nataraj misses final

Lawn bowls continue strong run

India ended Day 2 of the Commonwealth Games with one medal and several encouraging performances across para powerlifting, swimming, boxing and lawn bowls, as athletes continued to progress in their respective events.Jhandu Kumar opened India's medal account by winning bronze in the men's heavyweight para powerlifting event.The 28-year-old, who overcame polio, financial hardship and years of doing odd jobs before reaching the international stage, scored 130.9 points after successful lifts of 181kg and 190kg. He could not complete his final attempt of 196kg.The other Indian in the event, Sudhir, finished sixth with 114.1 points.Nigeria's Idris Riluwan won gold with 132.8 points, while Matthew Harding claimed silver with 131 points.India narrowly missed another medal in the men's lightweight para powerlifting event.Ashok Malik finished fourth with 143.8 points, missing out on a podium finish.England's Mark Swan won gold with 153.9 points. Nigeria's Roland Ezuruike (153.9) took silver, while Malaysia's Bonnie Bunyau Gustin (153.5) claimed bronze.India's Paramjeet Kumar finished seventh with 135.6 points.India came close to another medal when Karthik Budigina finished fourth in the men's 100m Freestyle S13 final.Budigina clocked 57.57 seconds, while teammate Imam Ali finished seventh in 1:03.73.South Africa's Nathan Hendricks won gold in 54.54 seconds. Scotland's Stephen Clegg took silver in 55.16 seconds and England's Matthew Redfern won bronze in 56.86 seconds.The S13 category is for athletes with visual impairments.Earlier in the day, both Budigina and Imam Ali had advanced to the final after all eight swimmers in the heats qualified. Budigina had finished third in the heats with a time of 57.10 seconds, while Imam Ali qualified with 1:05.32 seconds.Indian boxer Jadumani Singh made a winning start in the men's 55kg competition.He defeated Scotland's Aaron Cullen by unanimous decision in the Round of 32 to move into the pre-quarterfinals, where he will face Pakistan's Sumama Rehman.Srihari Nataraj's campaign in the men's 50m backstroke ended in the semifinals.The Indian swimmer finished seventh in his race with a time of 25.29 seconds and did not qualify for the final.South Africa's Pieter Coetze qualified fastest in 24.29 seconds, ahead of compatriot Ruard van Renen (24.56) and England's Oliver Morgan (24.65).India also enjoyed another successful day in lawn bowls.The women's pairs team of Rupa Rani Tirkey and Pinki Singh registered their second straight win, defeating South Africa 2-0 (6-4, 7-5) in their Section B match at the Scottish Event Campus Hall 3.In the men's singles, Putul Sonowal backed up his opening-day win over reigning world champion Ryan Bester of Canada with another hard-fought victory.The Assam Police officer defeated Falkland Islands' Cecil Alexander in a tie-break after the match ended 1-1 in sets.Sonowal recovered from a 3-4 deficit to win the opening set 7-5 before Alexander claimed the second set 8-6. The Indian then held his nerve in the tie-break to complete the win.
Article Summary: Jhandu Kumar wins bronze in men's heavyweight para powerlifting event. Karthik Budigina misses podium in para swimming. Jadumani Singh enters pre-quarterfinals of men's 55kg boxing event. Putul Sonowal wins men's singles at Commonwealth Games 2026.

Article Title: Commonwealth Games: India miss medal in first championship event as Ashok Kumar Malik finishes fourth in para powerlifting
Article Text:
India's Ashok competes in the Men's Lightweight Group A para powerlifting event at the 23rd Commonwealth Games, in Glasgow. (PTI Photo)

India missed out on a medal in the first championship event of the 2026 Commonwealth Games as Ashok Kumar Malik finished fourth and Parmjeet Kumar placed seventh in the men's lightweight para powerlifting competition on Friday.Ashok came closest to a podium finish but narrowly missed out despite producing two successful lifts.The competition featured athletes from multiple body-weight categories in a combined medal event. In such events, final rankings are decided using a coefficient formula that calculates points based on an athlete's body weight and their best successful lift.Parmjeet opened with a successful lift of 176kg, receiving two green lights and one red from the judges. He then attempted 179kg but failed to complete the lift.Ashok started strongly with a successful lift of 195kg, the heaviest opening lift in the field.In the second round, Parmjeet again went for 179kg but could not complete the attempt.Ashok then successfully lifted 200kg. The effort earned him 143.8 points and kept him in contention for a medal.Parmjeet made one final attempt at 179kg. Although he completed the lift, the judges ruled it invalid, awarding him three red lights.Ashok chose 205kg for his final attempt, which would have been the heaviest successful lift of his career. Even with a successful lift, however, he would have remained fourth because of the coefficient scoring system. He was unable to complete the attempt and finished fourth with 143.8 points.Parmjeet finished seventh with 135.6 points.England's Mark Swan won the gold medal with a score of 153.902.Nigeria's Roland Ezuruike claimed silver with 153.874 points, while Malaysia's Bonnie Bunyau Gustin took bronze with 153.5 points.
Article Summary: Ashok came closest to a podium finish but narrowly missed out despite producing two successful lifts. Parmjeet Kumar placed seventh in the men's lightweight para powerlifting competition on Friday. England's Mark Swan won the gold medal with a score of 153.902.Nigeria's Roland Ezuruike claimed silver with 153.874 points, while Malaysia's Bonnie Bunyau Gustin took bronze.

Article Title: 'She didn't disclose her whereabouts': JFI chief confirms Tulika Maan's CWG withdrawal, NADA hearing next
Article Text:
Tulika Maan (PTI Photo)

TimesofIndia.com

When Indian athletes faced similar cases

What is the whereabouts system?

Poll Vote & Share your view Do you believe the whereabouts system is effective in preventing doping violations? Yes, it helps maintain fairness. No, it's too complicated for athletes. 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

NEW DELHI: India's judo campaign at the 2026 Commonwealth Games in Glasgow has suffered another setback. A day after 73kg judoka Arun Kumar was ruled out after failing a dope test, CWG silver medallist Tulika Maan has been withdrawn from the Glasgow Games after coming under scrutiny over alleged whereabouts failures.spoke to Judo Federation of India (JFI) president Mukesh Kumar , who confirmed the development and said the matter is being looked into.Confirming the development, Kumar said: "She didn't tell us about her whereabouts. We are looking into this. As per the rules, an athlete needs to disclose his/her whereabouts to NADA. She didn't.""She has been called to the NADA office. She has gone there. We will talk to her. Let's see what decision comes up. But as an athlete, she had to disclose her whereabouts so that testing could be done on time," he said.Tulika is one of India's strongest medal hopes in judo at the Glasgow Games. She won a silver medal in the women's +78kg category at the 2022 Commonwealth Games in Birmingham. The Indian judo competition at the 2026 Games is scheduled from July 31 to August 2.The development comes just a day after when 73kg judoka Arun was declared ineligible following an adverse analytical finding in an out-of-competition test conducted by the National Anti-Doping Agency (NADA).Arun had enjoyed a rapid rise in recent years. He won gold at the 2023 Macau Junior Asian Cup, followed by another gold at the 2025 Taipei Asian Open and a bronze medal at the Hong Kong Asian Open. Earlier this year, he finished seventh at the prestigious Tashkent Grand Slam, earning his maiden Commonwealth Games selection.This is not the first time an Indian athlete has faced action over whereabouts failures.Sprinter Hima Das received a 16-month retrospective suspension by NADA after recording three whereabouts failures within a 12-month period (suspension ran from July 22, 2023, to November 21, 2025).Boxer Parveen Hooda was suspended by the International Testing Agency (ITA) for whereabouts failures (suspension ran from April 2022 and March 2023). She was also stripped of her bronze medal from the 2022 Asian Games .The whereabouts system is an anti-doping rule that allows authorities to carry out random, no-notice out-of-competition testing on elite athletes.Athletes who are part of a Registered Testing Pool (RTP) must submit their location details every three months through WADA's ADAMS platform or the Athlete Central app.They must also provide a fixed 60-minute time slot each day during which they will be available at a specific location for testing.If a doping control officer visits during that one-hour window and cannot find the athlete, it may be recorded as a missed test. Failing to submit or update location details is known as a filing failure.Under anti-doping rules, any combination of three missed tests or filing failures within a rolling 12-month period is treated as an anti-doping rule violation and can lead to a ban of one to two years.
Article Summary: Tulika Maan has been withdrawn from the 2026 Commonwealth Games. The development comes a day after 73kg judoka Arun Kumar was ruled out after failing a dope test. JFI president Mukesh Kumar confirmed the development and said the matter is being looked into.

Article Title: TOI Exclusive: Olympian Tulika Maan provisionally suspended by NADA, set to miss Glasgow CWG
Article Text:
India's Tulika Maan (PTI photo)

New Delhi:

India's Commonwealth Games campaign has suffered another major blow with Olympian and 2022 Birmingham CWG's silver medallist Tulika Maan being provisionally suspended by the National Anti-Doping Agency (NADA) for alleged whereabouts failures, ending her Glasgow 2026 participation even without flying out of India.Sources told TOI that Tulika, one of India's brightest medal prospects in the women's +78kg judo category, has accumulated three whereabouts failures within a rolling 12-month period, triggering a provisional suspension under the World Anti-Doping Agency (WADA) Code. She has been summoned by NADA and is scheduled to appear before the anti-doping body on Thursday.A whereabouts failure is an anti-doping rule compliance issue that includes filing failures and missed tests. A filing failure occurs when an athlete fails to submit or update mandatory location information for out-of-competition testing, while a missed test is recorded when a doping control officer is unable to locate the athlete during the declared 60-minute testing window. Any combination of three filing failures or missed tests within 12 months constitutes an anti-doping rule violation and carries a standard sanction of two years, unless successfully challenged.Tulika's provisional suspension comes as anotherblow to India's CWG preparations. The Indian contingent has now been reduced to 122 athletes, with the heavyweight judoka set to miss the Games after being provisionally suspended. The Indian judo team is scheduled to leave for Glasgow on July 27, with competitions beginning on July 31.The 27-year-old has been one of the leading faces of Indian judo over the past decade. Raised by her mother, Delhi Police sub-inspector Amrita, after losing her father at a young age, Tulika switched from football to judo at the age of eight before rising through the ranks under coach Yashpal Solanki.Her breakthrough moment came at the 2022 CWG in Birmingham, where she won a silver medal in the women's +78kg category, becoming only the second Indian judoka to achieve the feat. She later battled through a serious knee injury to qualify for the Paris Olympics, where she represented India as the country's lone judoka.The provisional suspension now casts a shadow over the career of one of India's most accomplished judokas, with the final outcome dependent on the proceedings before NADA. If upheld, Tulika could face a suspension of up to two years, dealing a significant blow to both her career and India's future medal hopes.
Article Summary: Tulika Maan has been provisionally suspended by the National Anti-Doping Agency. The 27-year-old is one of India's brightest medal prospects in the women's +78kg judo category. The Indian contingent has now been reduced to 122 athletes, with Tulika set to miss the Games.

Article Title: Historic first at Commonwealth Games as Braille medals debut in Glasgow
Article Text:
Militsa Milenkova the designer of the official medals for the 2026 Commonwealth Games poses with a medal (Getty Images)

Glasgow 2026 will make Commonwealth Games history by introducing medals featuring braille and tactile elements, ensuring visually impaired athletes can experience their achievements in a more inclusive way.The innovation marks the first time Commonwealth Games medals have been designed with braille, reflecting the organisers' broader commitment to accessibility and inclusion.That vision is also evident in the Games programme, which includes a record 47 gold medals across six Para sports, making it the largest Para sport programme in Commonwealth Games history. In total, athletes will compete for 215 gold medals across 10 sports and six Para sports.The medals themselves also break away from tradition in their appearance. Instead of the conventional circular design, they have been crafted in the shape of a Reuleaux triangle, inspired by Glasgow's coat of arms.Several elements of the host city's identity have been incorporated into the design. The engraved patterns draw inspiration from the Finnieston Crane, one of Glasgow's most recognisable landmarks and a tribute to the city's shipbuilding heritage.The textured finish reflects tartan, a symbol synonymous with Scotland, while the three raised levels on the medal represent the podium's first, second and third steps.The medal was created by award-winning artist Militsa Milenkova, who was born in Bulgaria and serves as an artist in residence at the Glasgow School of Art. Her concept was selected from submissions by students and artists from the institution's Silversmithing and Jewellery programme.Commonwealth Games medals have traditionally reflected the identity of the host city, and Glasgow's edition continues that tradition. At the same time, it sets a new benchmark by becoming the first medal in the event's history to include braille, making one of sport's greatest honours more accessible to every athlete who earns it.
Article Summary: Glasgow 2026 medals feature braille and tactile elements. First time Commonwealth Games medals have been designed with braille. Medals themselves also break away from tradition in their appearance. Instead of the conventional circular design, they have been crafted in the shape of a Reuleaux triangle.

Article Title: 'My best wishes to Indian contingent': PM Modi's message for Team India ahead of CWG 2026

PM Modi (ANI Photo)

India begins campaign with bowls events

Neeraj, Mirabai lead medal hopes

NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi wished the Indian contingent success ahead of the 2026 Commonwealth Games in Glasgow, expressing confidence that the athletes would compete with determination and inspire the nation.India begins its campaign on Thursday with a 124-member contingent looking to make a strong impact despite the reduced competition programme."As the Commonwealth #Glasgow2026 Games begin, my best wishes to the Indian contingent," PM Modi wrote on X."I am confident that our athletes will participate in the Games with passion, determination and a spirit of excellence. Article Title: After selling e-rickshaw to fund his dream, Jhandu eyes CWG medal
Article Text:
Bihar’s Jhandu Kumar

In 2021, during the Covid-19 pandemic, Bihar’s Jhandu Kumar drove an e-rickshaw to earn a living and support his family after he was forced to temporarily shut down the family-run vegetable shop at Harnaut Bazaar in Nalanda district due to the construction of an overbridge.It was a major setback to his sporting ambitions.Until then, despite financial struggles and being affected by polio from the age of five, he had managed to keep his dream alive by winning medals at state and national competitions in both para and able-bodied powerlifting.“Every day I used to travel nearly 20km to Bihar Sharif to buy vegetables, bring them back and sell them in the market. After finishing work around 4 pm, I would go to the gym for training,” Jhandu told TOI from Glasgow, where he will compete in the men’s heavyweight category of para-powerlifting on Friday.He followed that routine every day while training under Gautam Singh at Rockstar Gym. However, the money he earned was rarely enough to meet the demands of his diet.“I was earning only around ₹400-500 a day through my business, while protein supplements alone would cost nearly ₹1,000. Managing my diet and training was a huge challenge,” recalled the 29-year-old.Things became even more difficult after he started driving the e-rickshaw.Although it provided a steady income, the long hours left him too exhausted to train properly. Once the family was able to reopen the vegetable shop, he made another sacrifice to keep his sporting dream alive.“I sold my e-rickshaw in 2023 to participate in the National Para Powerlifting Championships,” said Jhandu.It was a huge gamble and, initially, it appeared to have backfired. He failed to register a successful lift at the competition in New Delhi. But his determination caught the attention of para powerlifting coach Rajinder Singh Rahelu, who invited him to train at the Sports Authority of India’s National Centre of Excellence in Gandhinagar.It proved to be the breakthrough he desperately needed. Later that year, he won a silver medal at the inaugural Khelo India Para Games in New Delhi.Since then, he has not looked back, winning medals at several national and international competitions, including a bronze medal at the Asia-Oceania Open Para Powerlifting Championships in Bangkok in April this year.He secured the podium with a 191kg lift, which also sealed his qualification for the Commonwealth Games. Besides these accomplishments, he also holds the national record in the 72kg category with a lift of 206kg.Now preparing for the biggest competition of his career, Jhandu credits the people who stood by him during the toughest phase of his journey, including his brother, Kundan.“I met people who supported and motivated me. I always believed that if I worked hard enough, I would achieve something. Financial support wasn’t always there, but I had confidence in myself. I kept telling myself that I would succeed one day,” he said.Making it to the Commonwealth Games in itself is a success for a man who never stopped believing in it. On Friday, Jhandu will hope to add a medal to that remarkable journey.Stay Updated With: CWG Schedule 2026
Article Summary: Jhandu Kumar will compete in the men's heavyweight category of para-powerlifting on Friday. The 29-year-old was affected by polio from the age of five. He has won medals at state and national competitions in both para and able-bodied powerlifting. He holds the national record in the 72kg category.

Article Title: Cape Verde's World Cup hero Vozinha finds new club; it's not Lionel Messi's Inter Miami
Article Text:
Vozinha and Lionel Messi

Cape Verde goalkeeper Vozinha has found a new club after his memorable FIFA World Cup campaign, signing for Colo Colo as a free agent. The move ends weeks of speculation linking the veteran shot-stopper with Lionel Messi 's Inter Miami during the summer transfer window.The 40-year-old was without a club after leaving Portuguese side Chaves on July 1. Following his standout performances at the World Cup, rumours suggested an MLS switch could be on the cards, with Inter Miami among the clubs reportedly interested.Instead, Vozinha has chosen to continue his career with Colo Colo, who announced the signing with the caption 'AURA' embedded in the announcement post on social media.The experienced goalkeeper became one of the biggest stories of the World Cup despite Cape Verde failing to win a match.Playing at the tournament for the first time in the nation's history, the Blue Sharks reached the Round of 32 after three gritty draws before narrowly losing 3-2 to defending champions Argentina after extra time.Vozinha was the standout performer throughout the tournament, producing a string of remarkable saves, particularly against Lionel Messi. The Cape Verde captain denied the Argentine superstar several times, almost helping his side pull off one of the biggest upsets in World Cup history."We have dignified Cape Verde as a national team in most parts of the world," Vozinha said after the defeat. "Today, we fought on an equal footing against Argentina."Cape Verde defender Pico Lopes was among those to praise the veteran goalkeeper, saying: "He's a quality, quality goalkeeper. Probably hasn't gotten the recognition he deserves before this. ... He's a legend in Cape Verdean football."Vozinha's career has largely been built through free transfers. He previously represented clubs including Chaves, AS Trencin, AEL Limassol, Gil Vicente, Zimbru Chisinau and Progresso before becoming a free agent this summer. Despite a reported market value of around €500,000, every move in his professional career has come without a transfer fee.With 92 international appearances since making his Cape Verde debut in 2012, Vozinha now begins a new chapter at Colo Colo, hoping to build on the global recognition he earned with his inspirational World Cup performances.
Article Summary: Cape Verde goalkeeper Vozinha has signed for Colo Colo as a free agent. The 40-year-old had been linked with an MLS move to Inter Miami. The veteran shot- stopper became one of the biggest stories of the World Cup. Cape Verde reached the Round of 32 after three gritty draws.

Article Title: Argentina's own FA sends blunt message after viral World Cup final replay petition passes 100,000 signatures
Article Text:
Argentina players react at the end of the World Cup final soccer match between Spain and Argentina in East Rutherford, N.J., near New York, Sunday, July 19, 2026. (AP Photo/Stephanie Scarbrough)

Replay petition gains traction online

Argentina players react at the end of the World Cup final soccer match between Spain and Argentina in East Rutherford, N.J., near New York, Sunday, July 19, 2026. (AP Photo/Stephanie Scarbrough)

Also read:

Claudio Tapia rejects replay demands

FIFA president Gianni Infantino, left, and Argentine Soccer Association President Claudio Tapia clap before the World Cup round of 32 soccer match between Argentina and Cape Verde in Miami Gardens, Fla., Friday, July 3, 2026. (AP Photo/George Walker IV)

Scaloni also dismissed conspiracy theories

Argentina head coach Lionel Scaloni reacts during the World Cup semifinal soccer match between England and Argentina in Atlanta, Wednesday, July 15, 2026. (AP Photo/Jacob Kupferman)

Also read:

Argentina FA urges fans to accept Spain's World Cup victory as viral replay petition tops 100,000 signaturesThe Argentine Football Association (AFA) has urged supporters to accept Spain's victory in the 2026 FIFA World Cup final after a fan-led petition demanding the match be replayed went viral in the days following Argentina's defeat in New Jersey.Spain secured their second men's World Cup title with a 1-0 extra-time victory over defending champions Argentina after Ferran Torres scored the decisive goal in the 106th minute at the New York New Jersey Stadium. Luis de la Fuente's side controlled much of the contest, while Argentina struggled to create chances and finished the match with 10 players following Enzo Fernández's late dismissal.The final has remained in the headlines ever since, not only because of the post-match altercation involving several Argentina players, but also because of growing conspiracy theories surrounding the officiating.An online petition launched on Change.org by Argentine supporter Gisela Sánchez has gathered more than 101,613 verified signatures, calling on FIFA to replay the World Cup final.The petition alleges that Slovenian referee Slavko Vinčić delivered a "controversial and corrupt" performance and asks FIFA to investigate several decisions made during the match.Its full description outlines concerns about the integrity of the officiating, claiming the final was overshadowed by alleged bias and questionable decisions.It argues that fans expect matches to be decided by skill and effort rather than refereeing calls, and warns that failing to address such concerns could damage trust in the sport.The petition also references videos circulating online that supporters believe show decisions favouring one side, and frames the issue as one that goes beyond Argentina, touching on the credibility of football globally.It concludes with a direct appeal to FIFA:“Therefore, we call upon FIFA to review these incidents with seriousness and transparency, and to consider replaying the final—this time without the influence of a corrupt referee.”However, no evidence has been produced to substantiate allegations that the referee or FIFA acted improperly, and there is nothing to suggest the match was influenced by bribery or corruption.Furthermore, petitions on Change.org carry no legal or sporting authority, and FIFA regulations provide for matches to be replayed only under extraordinary circumstances, not because of disagreement with refereeing decisions.Amid the growing online campaign, Argentine Football Association president Claudio "Chiqui" Tapia publicly distanced the federation from the replay calls and urged supporters to accept the result.In a lengthy statement shared on Instagram, Tapia acknowledged Spain's superiority on the day while encouraging fans to continue supporting the national team despite the disappointment."We were unable to get past Spain," Tapia wrote."We couldn't beat Spain. They were superior, they won fair and square, and we have to acknowledge that."He added that accepting defeat is part of elite sport."In sports, you also learn by accepting defeats with the same grace with which you celebrate victories."While admitting that losing another World Cup final was painful, Tapia reminded supporters that the squad had once again reached the biggest stage in international football."Yes, we lost a final. But it's also true that this group had just brought immense joy to the country.""Losing hurts. It hurts because we are competitive, because we are the most successful team in history, and because second place is never enough for us."The AFA president also defended the commitment shown by Lionel Scaloni's squad throughout the tournament."Let's think about the sacrifice of these players, the coaching staff, and every person who worked for more than 50 days away from their families, with a single objective: to represent Argentina in the best way possible."He concluded by warning supporters not to be influenced by misinformation."That's why you shouldn't be swayed by lies or by schemes that only seek to destabilise. Enough of trying to turn against those who have given so much to our football."Tapia's comments echo those made earlier by Argentina head coach Lionel Scaloni, who also rejected suggestions that Vinčić's officiating decided the outcome of the final.The Argentina manager acknowledged that Spain had simply been the better team on the night, despite disappointment over missing out on back-to-back World Cup titles.Ironically, Argentina themselves had faced repeated allegations of receiving favourable refereeing decisions earlier in the tournament. Among those to question FIFA's officiating was Egypt head coach Hossam Hassan, who claimed football's governing body wanted Lionel Messi and Argentina to remain in the competition for as long as possible.Despite the continuing debate online, FIFA has given no indication that the result of the World Cup final will be reviewed, with its ongoing investigation instead focused on the post-match altercations involving members of the Argentina squad following the final whistle.In addition to the replay petition, another viral campaign circulated online calling for Argentina to be stripped of their place in future World Cups, reportedly attracting around 23 million signatures before being taken down. Like the replay petition, it holds no official weight but highlights the intense global reaction to the controversial final.
Article Summary: Argentina FA urges fans to accept Spain's World Cup victory as viral replay petition tops 100,000 signatures. Petition alleges Slovenian referee Slavko Vinčić delivered a "controversial and corrupt" performance. No evidence has been produced to substantiate allegations that the referee or FIFA acted improperly, and there is nothing to suggest the match was influenced by bribery or corruption.

Article Title: Australia World Cup star Cristian Volpato reportedly tests positive for cocaine after being stopped twice in one night
Article Text:
Australia's Cristian Volpato reacts during the World Cup round of 32 soccer match against Egypt in Arlington, Texas, near Dallas, Friday, July 3, 2026. (AP Photo/Tony Gutierrez)

Stopped twice on the same night

Australia's Cristian Volpato arrives at the stadium ahead the World Cup round of 32 soccer match between Australia and Egypt in Arlington, Texas, near Dallas, Friday, July 3, 2026. (AP Photo/Sam Hodde)

World Cup campaign came after international switch

FILE -Sassuolo's Cristian Volpato controls the ball during the Serie A soccer match between AC Milan and Sassuolo at the San Siro stadium, in Milan, Italy, Dec. 30, 2023. (AP Photo/Antonio Calanni, File)

Tournament appearances for Australia

Australia international Cristian Volpato has reportedly tested positive for cocaine after being stopped twice by police for speeding in Sydney on the same night, just days after representing the Socceroos at the 2026 FIFA World Cup The 22-year-old Sassuolo midfielder was first stopped late on Thursday night before being pulled over again less than two hours later, when police allege he returned a positive roadside drug test for cocaine.The incident comes shortly after Volpato featured in Australia's World Cup campaign, having switched his international allegiance from Italy to Australia earlier this year before making three appearances at the tournament.According to reports, New South Wales Police said Volpato was first stopped at approximately 11:05 p.m. on Thursday while driving his BMW Coupe across Sydney's Anzac Bridge.Police allege he was travelling between 86 km/h and 94 km/h in a 60 km/h zone.A roadside breath test returned a negative result, and Volpato was issued with an infringement notice for speeding before being allowed to continue his journey.However, at around 1:10 a.m. on Friday, officers stopped the midfielder again in the same area after allegedly recording his vehicle travelling at 109 km/h in the 60 km/h speed zone—almost double the legal limit.Following the second stop, Volpato underwent a roadside drug test that allegedly produced a positive indication for cocaine.Police subsequently collected a secondary oral fluid sample, which has been sent for further laboratory analysis to confirm the result.His international driver's licence was also suspended for six months.Authorities have not announced any criminal charges relating to the alleged drug result while awaiting confirmation from the secondary test.Volpato's representatives have been approached for comment.The midfielder had only recently completed his first senior FIFA World Cup after making the decision to represent Australia instead of Italy.Born and raised in Sydney, Volpato developed through the youth systems of Sydney United 58, Sydney FC and Western Sydney Wanderers before moving to Europe as a teenager.He later progressed through Roma's academy before making his senior breakthrough in Serie A.Sassuolo signed the attacking midfielder in 2023, where he has since scored seven goals across three seasons.Before committing his future to Australia, Volpato had represented Italy at Under-19 and Under-20 level.As recently as March, he admitted he was still waiting for a senior Italy call-up after progressing through the country's youth teams. However, with Italy ultimately failing to qualify for the 2026 World Cup, the midfielder switched allegiance and accepted Australia's invitation.Volpato made three appearances during Australia's World Cup campaign in North America.He was an unused substitute as the Socceroos opened the tournament with a 2-0 victory over Turkey before coming off the bench during a 2-0 defeat to the United States.The 22-year-old then started Australia's goalless draw with Paraguay before also featuring in the Round of 32 meeting with Egypt.Australia's tournament came to an end after losing to Egypt in a penalty shootout, with Volpato substituted before extra time.The midfielder had been viewed as one of Australia's brightest emerging talents following his decision to represent the Socceroos, making the latest allegations an unwelcome development for both player and country.
Article Summary: Cristian Volpato has reportedly tested positive for cocaine after being stopped twice by police for speeding in Sydney on the same night. The 22-year-old Sassuolo midfielder was first stopped late on Thursday night before being pulled over again less than two hours later. Police allege he returned a positive roadside drug test for cocaine. The incident comes just days after he represented the Socceroos at the 2026 FIFA World Cup.

Article Title: Will Harry Kane stay? Bayern prepare talks as England captain enters final contract year
Article Text:
Bayern Munich's Harry Kane celebrates scoring during the Bundesliga soccer match between Borussia Dortmund and FC Bayern Munich in Dortmund, Germany, Saturday Feb. 28, 2026. (Federico Gambarini/dpa via AP)

Bayern keen to avoid losing Kane for nothing

Goals continue to flow in Germany

Bayern's Harry Kane celebrates after scoring during the DFB Pokal, German Cup final soccer match between VfB Stuttgart and Bayern Munich in Berlin, Germany, Saturday, May 23, 2026. (AP Photo/Ebrahim Noroozi)

Strong World Cup despite England heartbreak

England's Harry Kane (9) celebrates after scoring a goal during the World Cup Group L soccer match between England and Croatia in Arlington, Texas, near Dallas, Wednesday, June 17, 2026. (AP Photo/Tony Gutierrez)

Bayern planning for the future

Harry Kane is set to begin formal talks with Bayern Munich over a new contract as the Bundesliga champions look to secure the long-term future of one of the most prolific strikers in world football despite growing interest from rival clubs.Bayern are preparing to open negotiations with the England captain in the coming weeks, with the club eager to extend a deal that is currently due to expire at the end of the upcoming season.According to BBC Sport, The 32-year-old is understood to be fully aware of Bayern's intention to offer fresh terms, with discussions expected to progress after another outstanding campaign in Germany.Bayern's desire to tie Kane down comes as Europe's elite continue to monitor his situation.Barcelona have maintained a long-standing interest in the England international, while clubs from the Saudi Pro League have also been linked with a move for the striker.With Kane entering the final year of his current contract, Bayern are keen to avoid the possibility of losing one of their biggest stars on a free transfer next summer and are hoping a new agreement will reinforce his commitment to the club.Kane arrived in Munich from Tottenham Hotspur in the summer of 2023 in a deal reportedly worth £86 million and has since established himself as one of the most successful signings in Bayern's recent history.The move to the Bundesliga has coincided with arguably the most productive spell of Kane's career.Since arriving at the Allianz Arena, he has scored an extraordinary 146 goals in just 134 appearances across all competitions while helping Bayern win two Bundesliga titles and the DFB-Pokal.His most recent season proved especially remarkable.Despite approaching his 33rd birthday, Kane produced the finest goalscoring campaign of his career, scoring 61 goals in 51 appearances across all competitions to propel himself firmly into Ballon d'Or contention.His consistency has remained one of Bayern's greatest strengths, with the England captain continuing to combine elite finishing with creative play and leadership in attack.Kane also carried that form onto the international stage during the 2026 FIFA World Cup.The striker finished as one of England's leading scorer with six goals as Thomas Tuchel's side enjoyed their deepest World Cup run in decades before suffering heartbreak in the semi-finals.England appeared on course for the final before Argentina mounted a dramatic late comeback, with Lionel Scaloni's side scoring twice in the closing stages to secure a 2-1 victory and book their place in the final against Spain.England recovered to defeat France 6-4 in the third-place play-off, while Argentina ultimately fell short in the final after Ferran Torres' 106th-minute strike handed Spain a 1-0 extra-time victory and a second World Cup title.Although England narrowly missed out on reaching the final, Kane's performances throughout the tournament further enhanced his reputation as one of the world's leading forwards.Bayern's willingness to begin negotiations now underlines the importance they continue to place on Kane despite his age.Rather than viewing the striker as a short-term option, the German champions appear determined to build their next phase around the experienced forward, whose influence extends beyond his goalscoring record.For Kane, remaining in Munich would allow him to continue competing for major domestic and European honours while maintaining the exceptional form that has defined his time in Germany.Formal negotiations are now expected to begin in the coming weeks, with both club and player preparing to discuss the next chapter of a partnership that has already delivered goals, trophies and individual accolades at an extraordinary rate, according to BBC Sport.
Article Summary: Harry Kane is set to begin formal talks with Bayern Munich over a new contract. The 32-year-old is currently due to expire at the end of the upcoming season. Bayern are keen to avoid the possibility of losing one of their biggest stars on a free transfer next summer.

Article Title: Guardiola snubs Italy! Manager chooses personal break over rebuilding Azzurri after World Cup failures
Article Text:
Manchester City's head coach Pep Guardiola applauds supporters after the English Premier League soccer match between Manchester City and Bournemouth in Manchester, England, Sunday, Nov. 2, 2025. (AP Photo/Ian Hodgson)

Italy made Guardiola its priority

Brazil manager Carlo Ancelotti during a press conference at the Emirates Stadium, London, Friday, Nov. 14, 2025. (John Walton/PA via AP)

Guardiola sticks to long-term plan

Italy now turns to Plan B

La Gazzetta dello Sport

Rebuilding after unprecedented decline

Pep Guardiola has formally turned down the opportunity to become Italy's next national team manager despite the Italian Football Federation (FIGC) making him its leading candidate to rebuild the Azzurri after another disappointing FIFA World Cup campaign.The former Manchester City manager, who left the Premier League champions after a trophy-laden decade this summer, was approached by the FIGC following Italy's failure to qualify for a third consecutive FIFA World Cup. Although federation officials made an extensive effort to convince Guardiola to take charge, the Spaniard has instead decided to continue with his previously announced break from football.According to Italian newspaper La Gazzetta dello Sport , Guardiola thanked the federation for its confidence before politely declining the offer, telling officials: "I feel honoured, but at this moment it doesn't feel right."Italy have been searching for a new head coach since Gennaro Gattuso resigned in April following another failed World Cup qualifying campaign, extending one of the darkest periods in the country's modern football history.As previously reported , the federation initially explored the possibility of appointing Carlo Ancelotti before turning its attention to Guardiola.FIGC technical director Paolo Maldini later confirmed that Ancelotti was the federation's first choice."We cannot hide the fact that we also spoke to Carlo before talking to Pep," Maldini said during a news conference."Frankly, it seemed right to start with those we considered the best in the world."However, Ancelotti remained committed to Brazil after extending his contract through the 2030 FIFA World Cup, forcing Italy to pursue Guardiola instead.According to multiple Italian reports, Maldini and his advisor Leonardo held discussions with Guardiola over three days, presenting their long-term vision for restoring the national team to Europe's elite.The federation was reportedly even prepared to stretch its financial limits to secure one of football's most decorated managers, with FIGC president Giovanni Malagò previously revealing that "exceptions" could be made regarding Guardiola's salary.BBC Sport also reported that Italy were prepared to allow Guardiola significant freedom in shaping the project, effectively giving him considerable influence over the federation's footballing direction.Despite the ambitious proposal, Guardiola ultimately chose to remain faithful to the decision he announced before leaving Manchester City.The 55-year-old intends to spend time away from coaching, allowing himself the opportunity to rest, travel and spend more time with his family after nearly two uninterrupted decades in elite management.Speaking to Sky Sports a year before departing Manchester City, Guardiola had already indicated that a lengthy break was inevitable once his spell at the Etihad came to an end."No plans for [coaching] for a while. Otherwise I would be here. I need to step back. I will not [coach] for a while," Guardiola said during his final Manchester City press conference."I feel I will not have the energy every day, with expectations to fight for the title. I know myself, I have that energy, but I feel like I will not have it."In an earlier exclusive interview with Sky Sports, Guardiola also explained that his decision extended beyond football."There are things that I have not done that I want to do. I still have my father alive. I want to spend more time with him. My kids... And a lot of things as a human being I can do. I'm fortunate I can decide, that's why I took this decision."With both Ancelotti and Guardiola now unavailable, Italy's attention has shifted elsewhere.According to, former World Cup-winning midfielder Andrea Pirlo has emerged as the federation's preferred candidate and is expected to terminate his contract with Dubai-based United FC before finalising an agreement with the national team.The newspaper reports that Maldini and Leonardo believe Pirlo represents the right long-term figure to modernise Italian football and build a new identity rather than simply oversee the senior national side.The urgency surrounding the appointment is heightened by Italy's upcoming UEFA Nations League campaign, which begins in approximately eight weeks and includes fixtures against France, Belgium and Turkey, before attention turns toward qualification for UEFA Euro 2028 and ultimately the 2030 FIFA World Cup.Former Italy managers Roberto Mancini and Antonio Conte have also been linked with the vacancy.The search for a new coach comes during one of the most difficult periods in Italian football history.The four-time world champions have now failed to qualify for the 2018, 2022 and 2026 FIFA World Cups, despite lifting the UEFA European Championship under Roberto Mancini in 2021.Following the latest setback, the FIGC initiated a major restructuring by appointing Paolo Maldini and Leonardo to senior technical roles as the federation attempts to restore Italy's standing among world football's elite.
Article Summary: Pep Guardiola has formally turned down the opportunity to become Italy's next national team manager. The Italian Football Federation (FIGC) made Guardiola its leading candidate to rebuild the Azzurri after another disappointing FIFA World Cup campaign. The 55-year-old intends to spend time away from coaching, allowing himself to rest, travel and spend more time with his family after nearly two uninterrupted decades in elite management.
